primary_outcome_name: Time spent in moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) in bouts of >=10 minutes, at 36 weeks of gestation
primary_outcome_instrument_scale: Hip-worn accelerometry (ActiGraph GT3X+), Matthews' cut-points for MVPA classification, minutes/day (continuous)
primary_timepoint: 36 weeks of gestation (Visit 3; ~9 weeks after the end of the 12-week supervised exercise intervention)
arms: Exercise (individually supervised training, weeks 15-27 of gestation)
population_detail: Pregnant women with pre-pregnancy obesity (BMI >=30 kg/m2), singleton pregnancy, recruited before 14 weeks of gestation, randomised following baseline assessment (~14-15 weeks). Excluded if pre-existing diabetes or chronic hypertension. Recruited at CHU de Quebec and Centre de sante et de services sociaux de la Vieille-Capitale, Canada.

published_estimate.quote: Abstract, Results (p. 1): 'There was no time-group interaction for time spent at moderate and vigorous activity (pinteraction = 0.064), but the exercise group's levels were higher than controls' at all times (pgroup effect = 0.014).' Table 2 footnote a (p. 8): 'significant group effect, p = 0.014; values significantly higher in the exercise vs control group at all time[s]'. No point estimate (mean difference) or confidence interval is reported for the MVPA group effect anywhere in the paper -- only ANOVA interaction and main-effect p-values from the repeated-measures mixed model; Table 2 gives only the by-group, by-timepoint means +/- SD (MVPA in bouts, min/d: baseline 19.9+/-15.0 vs 16.8+/-17.6; 28 wk 25.4+/-20.4 vs 11.7+/-9.5; 36 wk 18.9+/-14.1 vs 9.5+/-9.8; p for interaction = 0.064).

B_covariate_list: None. The published primary model includes only group allocation (exercise vs control), time (14/28/36 weeks, as a 3-level factor) and the group x time interaction -- no covariate adjustment (e.g. for age, BMI, or parity) is reported anywhere in the Statistical Analyses section. Registry.csv's covars_published ('maternal_age, BMI_v1') do NOT correspond to any covariate actually used in the published primary analysis.
registration_id: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01610323 (registration submitted only after enrollment of the first participants had begun -- retrospective/delayed registration; at time of registration only 5 participants had completed the then-primary outcome assessment). Full study protocol (French and English versions) is deposited as Supporting Information (S1 Protocol, S2 Protocol), which is how the outcome switch documented below can be verified.
data_availability_statement: Data from the "Inter GO FIT" study are available from the Dryad Digital Repository (URL http://dx.doi.org/10.5061/dryad.87f03).

registry_check.issues: TWO separate mismatches identified. (1) OUTCOME-SWITCHING (registration vs. publication), explicitly disclosed by the authors themselves: 'At the time of registration, only 5 participants had completed the primary outcome assessment, which was originally cardiorespiratory fitness following the intervention as mentioned in the original protocol. However, cardiorespiratory testing in pregnant women with obesity raised feasibility issues, especially at 28 weeks, and accordingly the primary outcome was modified for the impact of the intervention on physical activity levels, in accordance with the registered protocol...' (Study design, p. 2-3). So the ORIGINAL protocol's primary outcome (cardiorespiratory fitness / VO2 at anaerobic threshold) was replaced, before/at registration, by a physical-activity primary outcome -- consistent with our registry note. (2) WITHIN the 'physical activity' domain, the registry's chosen analysis variable (Steps_per_day) is itself NOT the paper's designated primary outcome. The Methods explicitly state: 'The primary outcome was defined as the time spent at moderate and vigorous physical activity (MVPA) at 36 weeks of gestation' (Outcomes assessment, p. 4), and the a priori sample-size calculation (n=21/group) was powered specifically for this MVPA-in-bouts measure. Steps per day is only one of several secondary/exploratory accelerometry-derived variables reported alongside MVPA in Table 2 (others: counts/day, PPAQ self-reported energy expenditure) and is not mentioned at all in the Abstract. Furthermore, steps/day shows a WEAKER, non-significant between-group result (36-week between-group comparison p=0.072, i.e. only a trend) compared with the true primary outcome MVPA (significant group main effect p=0.014), so choosing steps/day instead of MVPA also changes the substantive headline finding that would be reanalysed. control_arm_matches is coded 'unclear' because paper.txt does not state the numeric coding of the 'Category' variable (exercise=?, control=?) used in the deposited Dryad_data.xlsx; this can only be verified by inspecting the deposited dataset directly, which was outside the scope of this paper-text-only extraction.

analysis_method_quote: Statistical analyses (pp. 4-5): 'Data are presented as means +/- standard deviation and percentage for continuous and categorical variables, respectively. Analyses were performed using SAS statistical package 9.4 on an intention-to-treat basis. In order to perform a comprehensive analysis of all physical activity measures over time (at 14, 28 and 36 weeks of gestation), repeated measures ANOVA using a linear mixed model were conducted to compare the effect of group allocation (exercise vs control), time (baseline, 28 weeks, 36 weeks) and their interaction on physical activity levels. If a significant "time-group" interaction was found, comparison over time was made for each group separately, and comparison between groups was made at each individual time. Otherwise, main effects were presented. The covariance structure for repeated measures ANOVA was chosen separately for each outcome. The structure with the lowest Akaike Information Criterion corrected for finite sample (AICc) amongst several of the most popular structures was chosen. The normality assumption of the residuals of the ANOVA was verified by checking the distribution of scaled residuals obtained by the linear mixed model. Skewness and kurtosis coefficients, as well as histograms and Kolmogorov-Smirnov and Shapiro-Wilk tests, were evaluated and confirmed that the assumption was met. Post hoc tests with the Bonferroni correction were performed to take into account multiple comparisons and keep the familywise error rate at 5%.'
notes: Preliminary/pilot RCT (explicitly labelled 'Preliminary Study' in the title); the a priori sample size (n=21/group, 50 recruited allowing 15% loss) was powered for the MVPA-in-bouts outcome, not for steps/day. Outcome-switching is TWO-LAYERED here: (a) protocol-to-registration switch, cardiorespiratory fitness (VO2 at anaerobic threshold) -> physical activity, openly disclosed by the authors in the Study design section as occurring because of feasibility problems with cardiorespiratory (treadmill) testing in obese pregnant women, and reportedly done 'in accordance with the registered protocol', i.e. before registration was finalised (registration itself was delayed, occurring only after some participants were already enrolled -- a further reporting-quality issue distinct from the outcome switch itself); (b) within-domain switch in our own registry coding, where Steps_per_day was selected as the outcome_var for reanalysis but the paper's actual primary outcome is MVPA in bouts >=10 min at 36 weeks -- a different accelerometry-derived variable with a materially different (stronger, significant) result than steps/day. n_analysed_primary=34 (18 exercise + 16 control) is the number with valid accelerometry data at the 36-week (primary) timepoint per Table 2; total accelerometry n's differ by timepoint (23/22 at 14 wk, 20/17 at 28 wk, 18/16 at 36 wk) because of drop-outs (n=5 overall, 10%) plus additional per-timepoint exclusions for insufficient accelerometer wear time (<8h/day or <5 days: n=5, 7, 11 excluded at 14/28/36 weeks respectively) -- since the primary analysis model is a mixed model (MMRM-type) using all available longitudinal observations under maximum likelihood, the effective analysed sample for the omnibus interaction/main-effect test may include participants with data at only some timepoints (up to n=45, i.e. all non-drop-outs), so 34 should be read as the complete-case n specifically at the 36-week primary timepoint, not necessarily the full analytic N contributing to the mixed-model result. No explicit statistical outlier rule (e.g. SD/IQR-based) is reported for the outcome distributions; the only exclusion criterion is accelerometer-wear-time-based data-quality filtering ('spurious data removed' via a published non-wear algorithm; <8h/day or <5 valid days excluded), coded here as B_outlier_rule='other' since it is a measurement-validity criterion rather than a statistical outlier rule on the outcome values themselves. Randomisation was stratified by parity, but the analysis model does not adjust for or otherwise mention parity, hence B_strat_factors_adjusted='no'. Baseline group differences were tested in Table 1 (e.g. age p=0.664, pre-pregnancy BMI p=0.684, both non-significant; total pre-pregnancy self-reported energy expenditure p=0.036, significant) but there is no indication the primary analysis model was modified in response to this baseline imbalance, hence C_adjust_after_baseline_test='no'. Journal is PLOS ONE, which has a long-standing mandatory Data Availability Statement policy for all research articles (consistent with the explicit Dryad-repository statement present in this paper), hence journal_requires_data_sharing coded 'yes' based on well-established PLOS editorial policy rather than an explicit in-text statement of the policy itself.
